questions.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order in the dataset, whatever its status (99,441 rows).

questions.question: How many sellers are on the platform?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) AS sellers
FROM sellers
questions.note: This counts every seller registered in the sellers table (3,095), whether or not they have made a sale.

questions.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviews
FROM order_reviews
questions.note: This averages every row in order_reviews, so a review that covers several orders is counted once per order.

questions.question: What is the total value of all payments in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_payments
FROM order_payments
questions.note: This sums every payment row with no order-status filter, because the question asks for all payments in the dataset (about 16.01M BRL), including those on canceled or unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the average price of an order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_item_price,
  COUNT(*)             AS items
FROM order_items
questions.note: This averages the price, excluding freight, over all order item rows regardless of order status, so each row counts as one unit.

questions.question: How many products are there in each product category (English names)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS products
FROM products
GROUP BY COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY products DESC, category
questions.note: This counts every catalogued product, whether or not it was sold, and groups products with no category under "unknown".

questions.question: How many distinct orders used each payment type?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, because the question is about payment usage rather than sales. An order paid with several methods is counted once under each type it used, so the per-type counts add up to more than the total number of orders.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders have the status delivered?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') / COUNT(*), 2) AS delivered_pct
FROM orders
questions.note: The denominator is every order with any status, canceled and unavailable included, because the question asks about "all orders."

questions.question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments,
    COUNT(*)                            AS credit_card_payments
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'
questions.note: This averages over all credit card payment rows, regardless of order status, because the question is about payment behaviour rather than sales.

questions.question: What is the average order value, measured as total payment per order, for orders that were not canceled or unavailable?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: Average order value is total payments divided by the number of distinct orders that have at least one payment row, so the single order with no payment is left out.

questions.question: What is the median total payment per order, across all orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SUM(payment_value) AS total_paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_paid)::numeric, 2) AS median_payment,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM order_totals
questions.note: I read "across all orders" literally, so no status filter is applied and canceled and unavailable orders are included; the median covers every order that has at least one payment row (the one order with no payment is left out).

questions.question: How many unique customers live in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers_rj
FROM customers
WHERE customer_state = 'RJ'
questions.note: This counts distinct people (customer_unique_id) with any RJ address, whether or not their orders were canceled. A person who also ordered from another state's address is still counted once here.

questions.question: How many products weigh more than 10 kg?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_over_10kg
FROM products
WHERE product_weight_g > 10000
questions.note: This counts catalog products whose weight is strictly above 10,000 g; products with no recorded weight are left out.

questions.question: How many order items cost more than 1,000 BRL?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_over_1000
FROM order_items
WHERE price > 1000
questions.note: This counts every item row (each row is one unit) whose price, excluding freight, is above 1,000 BRL, across all order statuses.

questions.question: How many delivered orders arrived after their estimated delivery date?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
questions.note: This counts orders with status 'delivered' and a recorded delivery date that falls after the estimated delivery date. Per the business rules, the result should be about 7,827.

questions.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sp_sellers
FROM sellers
WHERE seller_state = 'SP'
questions.note: This counts every seller registered in São Paulo (`seller_state = 'SP'`), whether or not they have made any sales.

questions.question: How many 1-star reviews include a comment message?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'reviews'
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) AS one_star_reviews_with_comment
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_score = 1
  AND review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(review_comment_message) <> ''
questions.note: This counts each review once by distinct `review_id`, because one review can cover several orders, and it treats blank or whitespace-only messages as having no comment.

questions.question: How many distinct orders were paid at least partly with a voucher?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS voucher_orders
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'voucher'
questions.note: This counts every order with at least one voucher payment row, including canceled and unavailable orders, because the question is about payment method rather than completed sales.

questions.question: How many products have no category?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category
FROM products
WHERE product_category_name_english IS NULL
questions.note: This counts every product in the catalog whose English category name is NULL. The schema says to expect about 610 such products.

questions.question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_seller_orders
FROM (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1
) t
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status (the dataset notes give 1,278); add a join to `orders` to exclude canceled or unavailable orders if you only want sales.

questions.question: List the cities in the state of Acre (AC) with the number of unique customers in each.
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'AC'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
questions.note: This counts distinct people (`customer_unique_id`) across all orders, with no order-status filter, because the question asks about customers rather than sales.

questions.question: How many orders were approved more than 24 hours after they were placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_approved_after_24h
FROM orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp > INTERVAL '24 hours'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status that have an approval timestamp, measured from purchase to approval; orders with no approval time are left out.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    s.seller_state AS state,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
    COUNT(*) AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue per seller is the sum of item prices without freight, counting only orders that are not canceled or unavailable.

questions.question: What is the total revenue by customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (payment_value, including freight and installment interest), and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: Which customer state has the highest average freight value per order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state                 AS state,
    COUNT(*)                         AS items,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2)  AS avg_freight_per_item
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY avg_freight_per_item DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This leaves out canceled and unavailable orders to follow the sales rule, and it averages freight over each order_items row, so each row counts as one unit.

questions.question: How many orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, because the question asks about orders placed rather than sales.

questions.question: Which 10 cities have the most unique customers?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city                        AS city,
    c.customer_state                       AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id)   AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I grouped by city and state so that different cities with the same name stay separate, and I counted people with `customer_unique_id` across all orders, regardless of order status.

questions.question: What is the average review score of orders paid with each payment type?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS order_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
order_types AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, payment_type
    FROM order_payments
)
SELECT
    ot.payment_type,
    COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(os.order_score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM order_types ot
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = ot.order_id
GROUP BY ot.payment_type
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
questions.note: Each order counts once per payment type it used, and orders with several reviews contribute the average of their scores. All order statuses are included because this is a satisfaction question, not a sales one.

questions.question: What was the total freight charged on items in the furniture_decor category?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'total_freight'
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(oi.freight_value), 2) AS total_freight,
  COUNT(*) AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'furniture_decor'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: I left out canceled and unavailable orders to match the sales rule. Remove that filter to get the total across all orders.

questions.question: What was the total revenue from customers in Minas Gerais (MG)?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS mg_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.customer_state = 'MG'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (payment values, including freight and interest), excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the English name of the product category 'cama_mesa_banho'?
questions.sql:
SELECT product_category_name AS category_pt,
       product_category_name_english AS category_en
FROM category_translation
WHERE product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
questions.note: This looks up the name in the translation table. The expected result is `bed_bath_table`.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest average review score among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
order_cats AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders
FROM order_cats oc
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY AVG(os.score) DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Each order's reviews are averaged first, and an order counts once for every distinct category it contains. All order statuses are included because this is a satisfaction question, not a sales one.

questions.question: Which 3 sellers have the highest average review score among sellers with at least 50 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS order_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, seller_id
    FROM order_items
)
SELECT
    so.seller_id,
    s.seller_state                    AS state,
    COUNT(*)                          AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(os.order_score), 2)     AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_orders so
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = so.order_id
JOIN sellers s       ON s.seller_id = so.seller_id
GROUP BY so.seller_id, s.seller_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC, reviewed_orders DESC
LIMIT 3
questions.note: I first average each order's reviews, since some orders have several. Each order counts once per seller, and orders of every status are included.

questions.question: How many unique customers bought from a seller located in a different state from their own?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c   ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN sellers s     ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND s.seller_state <> c.customer_state
questions.note: A customer counts if at least one item in a non-canceled, non-unavailable order came from a seller whose state differs from the customer's state on that order.

questions.question: What is the average price of items sold by sellers in each seller state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    s.seller_state                AS seller_state,
    COUNT(*)                      AS units_sold,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)       AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY avg_item_price DESC
questions.note: This averages the item price (without freight) over each unit sold, and leaves out canceled and unavailable orders because they don't count as sales.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each year?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed, whatever its status. Note that 2016 is very sparse (only Sep–Dec, mostly October) and 2018 effectively ends in August, so neither is a full year.

questions.question: Which month had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all orders of every status by purchase calendar month (year plus month); add `WHERE order_status NOT IN ('canceled','unavailable')` to count only sales.

questions.question: What was the average review score for each month of 2018, based on when the review was created?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', r.review_creation_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*)                                                         AS reviews,
    ROUND(AVG(r.review_score)::numeric, 2)                           AS avg_score
FROM order_reviews r
WHERE r.review_creation_date >= '2018-01-01'
  AND r.review_creation_date <  '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This averages over every review-order row in `order_reviews`, so a review that covers several orders counts once per order, and orders of every status are included. The order feed ends in August 2018, so the review counts for September and October will be small and partial.

questions.question: What was the total revenue in Q4 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_q4_2017
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-10-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue here is total customer payments (SUM of payment_value) for orders placed October–December 2017, with canceled and unavailable orders excluded.

questions.question: On which day of the week (e.g. Monday) are the most orders placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  to_char(order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay') AS day_of_week,
  COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY to_char(order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay')
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed, including canceled and unavailable ones, by the day of the week of its purchase timestamp.

questions.question: For each purchase month of 2017, what was the average delivery time in days (as a decimal) for delivered orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS purchase_month,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: Delivery time is measured as fractional days from purchase to customer delivery, and orders are grouped by the month they were purchased.

questions.question: How many orders were placed on Black Friday 2017 (November 24, 2017)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS orders_placed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS sales_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-11-24'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2017-11-25'
questions.note: `orders_placed` counts every order placed that day, whatever its status. `sales_orders` leaves out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule.

questions.question: Which product category had the largest increase in units sold from January–August 2017 to January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2017-09-01'
        ) AS units_2017,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
        ) AS units_2018
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    units_2017,
    units_2018,
    units_2018 - units_2017 AS unit_increase,
    ROUND(100.0 * (units_2018 - units_2017) / NULLIF(units_2017, 0), 2) AS pct_increase
FROM units
ORDER BY unit_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Units are counted as order_items rows, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: Which month of 2018 had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2019-01-01'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted orders by purchase month and left out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule. Data for 2018 effectively ends in August, so September and October are incomplete.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories had the largest drop in revenue from July 2018 to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-08-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS jul_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS aug_rev
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(jul_rev, 2) AS jul_revenue,
    ROUND(aug_rev, 2) AS aug_revenue,
    ROUND(jul_rev - aug_rev, 2) AS revenue_drop,
    ROUND(100.0 * (aug_rev - jul_rev) / NULLIF(jul_rev, 0), 2) AS pct_change
FROM cat_month
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(price) without freight, because the breakdown is by category; canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and products with no category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: What was the month-over-month percentage change in the number of orders for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
mom AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS mom_pct_change
FROM mom
WHERE month >= '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status, and uses December 2017 as the baseline so January 2018 also gets a change.

questions.question: For each customer state, which product category generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_state AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_state AS state,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN products p  ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_state, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        category,
        revenue,
        SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY state) AS state_revenue,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM cat_state
)
SELECT
    state,
    category AS top_category,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS category_revenue,
    ROUND(100.0 * revenue / state_revenue, 2) AS pct_of_state_revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY state
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(order_items.price) without freight, because the breakdown is by category; canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and ties within a state would return more than one row.

questions.question: What was the 3-month moving average of monthly revenue for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.paid) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
ma AS (
    SELECT month,
           revenue,
           AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month
                              ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_3m
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2)        AS revenue,
       ROUND(moving_avg_3m, 2)  AS moving_avg_3m
FROM ma
WHERE month >= '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: Revenue here is total payments (`payment_value`), excluding canceled and unavailable orders. The moving average is trailing: it covers the current month and the two before it, so January 2018 includes November and December 2017.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers had the highest item revenue in 2018, and what percentage of total 2018 item revenue did each account for?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
)
SELECT sr.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       ROUND(sr.revenue, 2) AS item_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * sr.revenue / SUM(sr.revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_2018_revenue
FROM seller_rev sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
ORDER BY sr.revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Item revenue is SUM(price) without freight, counting only sale orders (not canceled or unavailable) by purchase date. The percentage is computed against all sellers' 2018 revenue before the LIMIT is applied. 2018 data effectively ends in August.

questions.question: For 2017 and 2018 separately, what were the top 3 product categories by units sold?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_units AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) AS units_sold
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        category,
        units_sold,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY units_sold DESC, category) AS rank
    FROM cat_units
)
SELECT year, rank, category, units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3
ORDER BY year, rank
questions.note: Units sold are counted as order_items rows from orders that are not canceled or unavailable. Note that 2018 is incomplete: the data effectively ends in August 2018, so the two years are not fully comparable.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY pct_of_orders DESC
questions.note: Because the question says "all orders," this counts every order regardless of status, including canceled and unavailable ones.

questions.question: Which month in 2017 had the largest increase in orders compared with the previous month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
changes AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       orders - prev_orders AS increase,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / prev_orders, 2) AS pct_increase
FROM changes
WHERE prev_orders IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all orders placed regardless of status, and compares only within 2017, so January is excluded because December 2016 has just 1 order and would create an artificial spike.

questions.question: For each seller state, which seller has the highest revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT
        s.seller_state,
        oi.seller_id,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY s.seller_state, oi.seller_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        seller_state,
        seller_id,
        revenue,
        orders,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM seller_rev
)
SELECT
    seller_state AS state,
    seller_id,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    orders
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales (SUM of price, without freight), because payments can't be split by seller. Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and if two sellers tie for first in a state, both are shown.

questions.question: What was our revenue in 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_2017
FROM order_payments p
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue here is the default order-level measure: the total customers paid (payment_value, which includes freight and installment interest) on 2017 orders, excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the average delivery time?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
questions.note: Delivery time is measured in days, from when the customer placed the order to when they received it, using only delivered orders that have a delivery date.

questions.question: What was revenue by state in 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state                  AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)        AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2)            AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue is what customers paid (payments, including freight and installment interest), grouped by the customer's state and excluding canceled and unavailable orders. Note that 2018 data effectively ends in August, so the year is incomplete.

questions.question: How are we doing?
questions.sql:
WITH o AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           customer_id,
           order_status,
           date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp) AS mon,
           order_delivered_customer_date,
           order_estimated_delivery_date,
           order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') AS is_sale
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
),
pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
rev AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT o.mon,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_sale) AS orders,
           SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE o.is_sale) AS revenue,
           COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) FILTER (WHERE o.is_sale) AS customers,
           AVG(r.score) AS avg_review,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
                              AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) AS delivered,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
                              AND o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS late
    FROM o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY o.mon
)
SELECT to_char(mon, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY mon))
             / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY mon), 0), 2) AS revenue_mom_pct,
       ROUND(revenue / NULLIF(orders, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value,
       customers,
       ROUND(avg_review, 2) AS avg_review,
       ROUND(100.0 * late / NULLIF(delivered, 0), 2) AS late_delivery_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY mon
questions.note: I read "how are we doing" as a monthly KPI scorecard covering orders, payment revenue, month-over-month growth, AOV, unique customers, review score and late-delivery rate, limited to the reliable months from 2017-01 to 2018-08.

questions.question: Who are our best customers?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT op.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments op
    GROUP BY op.order_id
),
sales AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           o.order_id,
           o.order_purchase_timestamp,
           COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS paid
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
)
SELECT customer_unique_id                              AS customer,
       COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)                        AS orders,
       ROUND(SUM(paid), 2)                             AS total_spent,
       ROUND(SUM(paid) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2)  AS avg_order_value,
       MIN(order_purchase_timestamp)::date             AS first_order,
       MAX(order_purchase_timestamp)::date             AS last_order
FROM sales
GROUP BY customer_unique_id
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I read "best customers" as the top 10 people (by customer_unique_id) ranked by total amount paid, counting only orders that are not canceled or unavailable.

questions.question: What was the recent trend?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS customers,
        SUM(COALESCE(p.paid, 0)) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-09-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    orders,
    customers,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    ROUND(revenue / NULLIF(orders, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS revenue_mom_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * (orders - LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS orders_mom_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
questions.note: I read "recent trend" as monthly sales (orders, unique customers, payment revenue, average order value, and month-over-month change) for the last 12 reliable months, Sep 2017 to Aug 2018. The query excludes canceled and unavailable orders, and it leaves out 2018-09/10 because those months have almost no data.

questions.question: What is the age distribution of our customers?
questions.sql:
WITH sales_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp, c.customer_unique_id
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
ref AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS ref_ts FROM sales_orders
),
first_purchase AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id, MIN(order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_ts
    FROM sales_orders
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
),
tenure AS (
    SELECT fp.customer_unique_id,
           EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.ref_ts - fp.first_ts)) / 86400.0 AS tenure_days
    FROM first_purchase fp
    CROSS JOIN ref r
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT CASE
             WHEN tenure_days < 90  THEN 1
             WHEN tenure_days < 180 THEN 2
             WHEN tenure_days < 365 THEN 3
             WHEN tenure_days < 545 THEN 4
             ELSE 5
           END AS bucket_order
    FROM tenure
)
SELECT CASE bucket_order
         WHEN 1 THEN '0-3 months'
         WHEN 2 THEN '3-6 months'
         WHEN 3 THEN '6-12 months'
         WHEN 4 THEN '12-18 months'
         ELSE '18+ months'
       END AS tenure_band,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_customers
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY bucket_order
ORDER BY bucket_order
questions.note: The dataset has no birth dates or ages, so this query shows a proxy instead: customer tenure. Tenure is the time since each person's first non-canceled purchase (counted by customer_unique_id), measured up to the last purchase date in the data. Real demographic ages cannot be computed from this database.

questions.question: Which marketing campaign brought in the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT op.order_id,
           SUM(op.payment_value) AS paid,
           BOOL_OR(op.payment_type = 'voucher') AS used_voucher
    FROM order_payments op
    GROUP BY op.order_id
)
SELECT CASE WHEN p.used_voucher THEN 'voucher_used' ELSE 'no_voucher' END AS segment,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(p.paid) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM order_pay p
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note:
The database has no marketing campaign, channel, UTM or attribution data, so it can't say which campaign brought in the most revenue. The closest proxy is whether an order was paid partly with a **voucher**, which may reflect promotions. This query compares revenue for orders with and without a voucher:

Vouchers can also be store credit or refunds, so treat this only as a rough promotional signal, not as campaign attribution.
